name: 2003 invasion of Iraq (Operation Iraqi Freedom, major combat)

sides.name: Coalition (US, UK, Australia, Poland)
sides.note: Strength: 589,799 coalition personnel total incl. naval/air and 70,000 Peshmerga (Wikipedia infobox); ~250,000 soldiers massed on the Kuwait border (On Point); 1,800 coalition aircraft (On Point); 101st Airborne alone self-deployed >250 helicopters (On Point). Ground manoeuvre: 3rd Infantry Division, 101st Airborne, 82nd Airborne elements, 1st Marine Division, Task Force Tarawa, UK 1st Armoured Division, 3 Commando and 16 Air Assault Brigades. infantry_line (dismounts), armour, ifv_apc, artillery and helicopter counts are educated reconstructions from that order of battle (no fetched source gives the totals; grade D for these). Fighter/strike split of the 1,800 aircraft (which include tankers and support) educated. Kurdish Peshmerga and northern SOF are outside the theatre and excluded. Reinforcement day 23: 4th Infantry Division entering from Kuwait mid-April, educated. Starts: V Corps in western Kuwait, I MEF and UK in eastern Kuwait, SOF in the western desert. Doctrine us-joint-2026 is the closest available id (networked joint precision warfare), not a claim of 2026 capability. Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 2003 between 9 and 10): JDAM, Javelin, Blue Force Tracker, Predator. Ratings: command 0.85; morale 0.75; training 0.9 (long-service volunteers). Surprise: G-day preceded the air campaign (On Point).

sides.name: Iraq (Regular Army, Republican Guard, Fedayeen Saddam)
sides.note: Strength: Army 280,000-350,000 in 17 divisions, Republican Guard 50,000-80,000, >2,200 tanks, 2,400 APCs, 4,000 artillery pieces (On Point Figure 45); IISS: ground forces 350,000, Fedayeen Saddam 44,000; other estimate Fedayeen 20,000-40,000 (Wikipedia). infantry_line excludes crews and the northern corps facing the Kurds only partly (educated ~65-75% of army + RG); infantry_light = Fedayeen and Ba'ath militia. Air force did not fly, so no aircraft listed. Starts: III Corps at Basra, 11th Division at Nasiriyah, IV Corps at Amarah, RG Baghdad Division at Kut, Medina/Nebuchadnezzar at Karbala-Hillah, Baghdad, militia at Najaf/Samawah, Tikrit. Tech: 1970s-80s Soviet kit degraded by sanctions; ISR 7 (no air reconnaissance); cyber 7 educated (outside the anchor table). Ratings: command 0.2 (Saddam's interference, RG mispositioned); morale 0.3 (regular army melted away; Fedayeen fanatical); training 0.35. Not fortified: no prepared defence of Baghdad.

outcome.note: 20 March - 9 April 2003 (Baghdad, day 21); Tikrit taken 15 April (day 27). Coalition: 172 killed (139 US, 33 UK), 551 US wounded, Peshmerga 24+ killed (Wikipedia), a handful captured. Iraq: combatant fatalities 7,600-10,800, best estimate ~9,200 (Project on Defense Alternatives); Wikipedia range 11,000-45,000; >7,300 EPWs in coalition custody on 9 April (On Point); wounded unknown (educated ~1.5-2.5x killed). Many soldiers simply went home and are not counted as losses. Grade C on losses.
